answer: Hardware Enclave Memory Isolation Each agent runs inside a processor enclave tied to a physical motherboard at the wharf. Compromising this boundary trips a thermal sensor, which permanently bricks the silicon fuse. The attacker loses the host hardware unit and pays the retail replacement cost for every banned identity node. Meanwhile, a background thread monitors network chatter like a distant lantern, checking execution cadence. If duplicate routines emerge across ports, the system triggers a memory purge, shredding the internal lotus encryption keys required to decrypt task payloads.
